result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-024 (/my registrations view with live status, computed waitlist position and the QR pass, GitHub issue #27) at commit 36a17e1, branch feature/WF02-REQ-024 -- the LAST requirement of Phase 4. Did not trust TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report, the test report, or requirement_status.yaml history as substitutes for my own re-derivation. 1. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-024.md in full against all 5 acceptance criteria (§6's AC-to-design-element map). Every AC maps to a concrete, non-deferred design element; §5's 3 open questions (pagination, ci_ deep-link consumption at check-in time, per-row send-failure UX) are named explicitly rather than silently resolved, and none of the 5 ACs in scope depend on them. Confirmed 'no schema change' myself: git diff master...HEAD --stat -- apps/bot/drizzle produced zero output. 2. Read apps/bot/src/domain/qr.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's getMyRegistrations (lines 594-650), and apps/bot/src/handlers/my.ts in full, comparing line-by-line against the design: the exact deep-link template (https://t.me/?start=ci_), the single userId-only parameter on getMyRegistrations with no second caller-suppliable identifier anywhere in its signature, the QR gate (admission==='admitted' && qrToken!==null) as the sole predicate deciding replyWithPhoto vs. plain reply, the withdraw-button eligibility computed via decideWithdrawOutcome (REQ-022, reused unchanged, ownerUserId===actingUserId always by construction), and one message per row. Confirmed STATUS_CATALOG_KEY was exported from handlers/registration.ts with no other export/behavior change to that file. 3. Re-ran npm run lint myself: 0 errors, 2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx, Nav.tsx) -- unrelated to this diff, matches TEST-RUNNER's report. Re-ran npm run build myself: apps/web (Next.js/Turbopack) compiled successfully; apps/bot (tsc -p tsconfig.json) clean, zero errors. Re-ran npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism from the repo root myself: first without a reachable scratch Postgres (19 files, 171 passed / 46 skipped = 217 total, confirming the DB-suite's self-skip guard fires correctly), then again after standing up my own scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432) and running npx drizzle-kit migrate myself (applied cleanly, zero new migration files) -- second run: 19 files / 217 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed. Matches TEST-RUNNER's reported 217-test count exactly. 4. Independent re-verification of AC1, AC2, and AC3 (plus an end-to-end integration sanity check), using my own fixtures against my own scratch Postgres, my own harness (apps/bot/scratch-rv-req024.ts, written fresh, never reusing BACKEND-DEV's or TEST-RUNNER's scratch harnesses or handlers/my.test.ts's fixtures), deleted after the run (git status --porcelain confirmed clean before this handoff): - AC1 privacy scan: capacity-1 event, SECRET user registered first (fills the seat, admitted) with a full 5-field profile (SuperSecretFirst/SuperSecretLast/TopSecretCompany/+19995551234/supersecret@example.com), VIEWER registered second (waitlisted). Scanned VIEWER's full captured /my payload set for 7 needles (5 profile fields, SECRET's raw Telegram id, SECRET's internal user id) -- none present; VIEWER's own event title WAS present (sanity that the scan itself is meaningful). PASS. - AC2 live waitlist position, real REQ-023 auto-promotion path: capacity-1 event, SEATHOLDER admitted, AHEAD waitlisted position 1, VIEWER waitlisted position 2 (all via real register: callback dispatch). VIEWER's /my read position 2. Real /withdraw command + parsed real confirm button + real withdraw:confirm: callback dispatch for SEATHOLDER. Confirmed AHEAD (not VIEWER) was auto-promoted to admitted by reading the DB row directly. VIEWER's /my then read position 1. VIEWER's own registration row's updated_at was byte-identical (ISO-string compared) before and after, admission still exactly 'waitlisted'. PASS. - AC3 real QR decode: one MEMBER registered for two distinct capacity-5 events via real register: callbacks, producing two distinct qr_tokens (confirmed non-equal at the DB level). /my sent exactly 2 sendPhoto calls. Decoded both raw PNG buffers with real jsqr+pngjs (extracted from grammY's InputFile.fileData directly, not from a stub): each decoded to exactly https://t.me/rv_test_bot?start=ci_, correctly paired to its own registration, no cross-row mix-up. PASS. - End-to-end Phase-4 integration sanity (task step 6): using the same MEMBER and the same two real registrations from the AC3 fixture, dispatched /my again, parsed the real withdraw:confirm: button rendered on one of the admitted rows, and dispatched that exact real callback_data through the bot -- confirmed the underlying registration's admission flipped to 'withdrawn' in the database. Re-ran /my once more: exactly 1 sendPhoto call remained (only the still-admitted row), confirming the withdrawn row correctly stopped rendering a QR image. This exercises the full chain register -> /my (QR render) -> /my's own withdraw button -> withdraw -> /my (updated view) against real code and a real database, with no direct DB inserts standing in for any step. 5. Confirmed full requirement scope: git diff master...HEAD --stat shows exactly the files the design describes (apps/bot/package.json, domain/qr.ts + its test file, domain/registration.ts, handlers/my.ts + its test file, handlers/registration.ts's one-line export addition, i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts, index.ts's 2 new registrations, docs/design, docs/test-specs, docs/issues/ISS-0021.yaml, plus this run's own handoffs/test-report) -- nothing stray. Grepped apps/bot/src for TODO/FIXME/XXX (excluding test files): zero matches. Confirmed qrcode (1.5.4, dependencies), jsqr (1.4.0), pngjs (7.0.0), @types/pngjs (6.0.5), @types/qrcode (1.5.6) are all exact-pinned (no ^ or ~) in apps/bot/package.json -- all 5 of this requirement's new dependencies. git status --porcelain clean (scratch file and scratch Postgres container/volume torn down after use). All design-doc-listed files present and match the design's reused-vs-new list exactly. 6. Phase 4 coherence sanity check: read requirement_status.yaml's REQ-019 through REQ-023 history entries -- all five are marked done, each an independently RELEASE-VALIDATOR-passed step in one coherent registration lifecycle (REQ-019 profile capture -> REQ-020 register with atomic capacity + qr_token issuance -> REQ-021 live waitlist position -> REQ-022 withdraw and free the seat -> REQ-023 auto-promotion on a freed seat -> REQ-024 this run's /my view surfacing all of it, including the first-ever QR-image delivery). My own end-to-end integration run in step 4 above is not a mere plausibility argument -- it is a live re-derivation that /my's withdraw button, on a registration created via the real /register flow, genuinely triggers REQ-022's real withdrawRegistration() and REQ-023's real promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible() path (independently confirmed by AC2's own AHEAD-gets-promoted check), and that the QR pass this same view renders decodes to the exact deep-link REQ-026's future check-in flow will need. No integration gap found between any of the six requirements' surfaces. Overall: every independent check I ran -- lint, build, full test suite from the repo root (with and without DB), an independently-constructed AC1 privacy scan, AC2 live-position/no-write check riding the real REQ-023 promotion path, AC3 real jsqr+pngjs decode of two independently produced QR images, and a fresh end-to-end register->/my->withdraw integration run -- agrees with all seven prior gates (CODE-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, BACKEND-DEV, REVIEWER, SECURITY-REVIEWER, TEST-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, TEST-RUNNER). No half-implemented scope, no stray TODOs, clean git tree, all design-doc-listed files present, all 5 new dependencies exact-pinned. Phase 4 (REQ-019 through REQ-024) forms a coherent, complete registration lifecycle with no obvious integration gap.

issues.description: Carried forward from TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report, independently re-confirmed here: docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-024.md's AC5 grep-based pass condition ('exactly one line') does not account for domain/qr.ts's own header comment echoing the ?start=ci_ literal alongside its actual code use -- both lines are inside domain/qr.ts, so there is no functional duplication (the property AC5 exists to protect), but the spec's wording is imprecise. This is the same class of issue as ISS-0021 (filed this run by a prior step for a related AC5 wording nit). No action needed for this release; recommend TEST-DESIGNER tighten the wording on a future spec revision.
